title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཟེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 191)
shelf_note: Correctly cataloged under Pramāṇa in the Derge Tengyur (vol. 191, volume mark 'ze').

ocr_errors.problem: vowel sign misread (drengbu 'e' misread as giku 'i') in the name of the wild ox / gayal (gavaya)

tr_errors_B.english: For example, just as when a location is perceived and fire itself is remembered, is it not the case that it becomes the object of a distinguished valid cognition of inference <term>anumana</term>?
tr_errors_B.problem: Turns a declarative assertion that inference is valid despite having a qualified object into an awkward rhetorical question, weakening the philosophical point of the double negative (ma yin min).

tr_errors_B.english: since universals <term>samanya</term> have been refuted, how could those parts be many or have such a connection?
tr_errors_B.problem: Misidentifies the pronoun referent 'de dag la' (in them) as referring to the parts rather than to the refuted universals.

pages.prefer_reason: Translation A exhibits superior philosophical accuracy and fluency in classical Buddhist epistemological terminology, correctly translating the double negative in the inference analogy and accurately resolving pronoun references.

book_verdict: Clear and complete scan of a Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa folio discussing the epistemological status of comparison (upamāna), with near-flawless OCR and an accurate, philosophically adept translation in version A.
